messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test `testNestedDOM()` in `XMLSpaceTest` expects that when querying an XML document for a text node, the string values retain their original leading and trailing spaces (i.e., string values are not trimmed). The test does this by calling `doTest("nested", DocumentContainer.MODEL_DOM, "foo;bar; baz ")`. The summary of the bug report states that JXPath automatically trims string values, for example returning `"1234 56"` instead of `" 1234 56"` when querying XML data containing whitespace.

From the test code and helper method `doTest()`, it obtains a `JXPathContext` on a document created with the model "DOM". The document is loaded from an XML resource ("XmlSpace.xml") into a `DocumentContainer` constructed with the model string `MODEL_DOM`. The `DocumentContainer` constructor simply stores the URL and model string.

The key step is how the XML is parsed and turned into a DOM document. The `DocumentContainer` method `getValue()` lazily parses the XML by calling `parseXML()`, which in turn delegates to an `XMLParser` chosen by the model. If the parser is of type `XMLParser2`, certain parser configuration flags are set, including a flag called `setIgnoringElementContentWhitespace()`.

This parser configuration flag is critical, as it controls whether the XML parser ignores ignorable whitespace (whitespace in element content). When this is set to true, leading and trailing spaces in text nodes will typically be ignored or trimmed by the parser itself. Therefore, even before JXPath applies any logic, the DOM node content will have lost the original whitespace, causing `JXPathContext.getValue()` to reflect trimmed text.

Hence, the root cause of the bug is that the XML parser used by `DocumentContainer` has "ignoring element content whitespace" enabled, causing it to trim leading and trailing spaces in XML text values. This is why JXPath returns trimmed string values, which contradicts user expectations per the test.

No recent bug reports pointed out a different issue, so the diagnosis centers on the parser configuration flag `setIgnoringElementContentWhitespace` causing the loss of whitespace during XML DOM creation. The fix would involve either disabling this flag or preserving white space semantics during XML parsing to keep original text spacing intact.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
